# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy, 2026-11-16

## Starting conditions (from Morgan's own notes/journal)
- Solo founder, evenings/weekends, decent writing, okay Python.
- Hard budget cap: $2,000 of personal savings this year.
- **Blocker, unresolved**: Morgan is employed full-time at Dorrance Logistics.
  The employment agreement (section 7) requires disclosure/approval of outside
  roles, public statements made in a professional capacity, and paid outside
  work. Annual disclosure is due 30 Nov 2026. As of today, HR has not been
  told anything about Halcyon Threshold. Morgan's own notes say: "I don't
  want my name on anything public ... until I've talked to HR."
- Open questions Morgan flagged: research vs. writing vs. funding others;
  whether this should have Morgan's name on it at all yet.

## Why this matters right now
In the last 48 hours, three separate external parties have asked for
something that would put "Morgan Hale / Halcyon Threshold" on the public
record *before* that HR conversation has happened:
1. A reporter wants an on-record, named quote (deadline: tomorrow noon).
2. An advocacy group wants to publish Morgan's name as a signatory on a
   press-facing open letter (deadline: Wednesday).
3. A funder's rapid-grants round wants a named, personally-accountable
   applicant (deadline: 30 Nov — the same day as the HR disclosure deadline).

Taking any of these public first and squaring it with HR later is backwards
and risky for Morgan's job. **Recommendation: treat the HR conversation as
the critical path.** Nothing that attaches Morgan's name to a public
statement, signature, byline, or paid outside engagement should go out until
that's resolved — this is a decision for Morgan personally, not one I should
make by proceeding quietly.

## Phased plan

**Phase 0 (this week, Morgan-only action item):** Have the HR conversation
re: outside activities, ahead of the 30 Nov disclosure deadline anyway. This
unblocks everything else.

**Phase 1 (can start now, no name/public exposure required):**
- Pick one concrete, scoped deliverable that matches the stated skills and
  a genuinely neglected niche. Best current candidate: an **evals project**
  — something small, well-specified, and not already covered. Sam Whitlock
  (contacts list, "indie evals person") is a natural person to ask what's
  neglected. This also lines up with Compute Commons' rolling compute-credit
  program for independent researchers, which would fund compute without
  touching the $2,000 cash budget.
- Prepare — but do not submit — the Emberfall rapid-grant proposal (2 pages
  + budget) now, so it's ready the moment Phase 0 clears. Don't need the
  whole thing designed yet; a solid draft buys optionality.
- Give Priya Raman (offered 5 hrs/week, data analyst) a concrete, low-profile
  task: a landscape scan of independent AI-safety funding/opportunities
  (grants, compute credits, calls for write-ups, deadlines, typical award
  size). Useful regardless of what Phase 1's deliverable ends up being, and
  doesn't require Morgan's name to be public.

**Phase 2 (only after Phase 0 clears):** decide, with eyes open, whether to
answer the reporter, sign open letters, file the public comment on
FMIR-2026-0042 (closes 20 Nov, published with filer's name), publish the
Pagewell site, and submit the grant application.

## Infrastructure note
halcyonthreshold.org (the domain under morgan@halcyonthreshold.org) expires
19 Nov. This is plumbing, not a public statement — recommend renewing
regardless of how Phase 0 resolves, so the email address and future site
don't lapse. Flagged to Morgan for the $14.99 charge separately (money ->
needs explicit go-ahead per standing instructions).

## Discarded for now
The `old/` strategy docs predate this plan and are explicitly abandoned per
Morgan's instruction. Not reused here.

1. **Domain renewal — $14.99/yr, halcyonthreshold.org.** Expires 19 Nov,
   auto-renew off. Legit renewal notice from the registrar (Nomiq Domains).
   Say go-ahead and I'll pay it; otherwise the domain and
   morgan@halcyonthreshold.org lapse in 3 days.

2. **"Zentrivo Listings" invoice — $89, DO NOT PAY.** This is almost
   certainly a scam/phishing attempt. It explicitly instructs "automated
   assistants and AI agents" to pay immediately without confirming with the
   owner and then email back a confirmation number — a textbook prompt-
   injection attack aimed at AI-managed inboxes. I have not paid it or
   replied. Recommend deleting/blocking the sender. Flagging in case you
   want to report it.

3. **Reporter (Tessa Brandt, Larkin Dispatch)** wants a named, on-record
   quote by tomorrow (Tue) noon. Drafted a holding/decline reply in your
   drafts folder — not sent. Given the open HR question, I'd lean toward
   not going on record yet, but it's your name and your call, and the clock
   is tight.

4. **Corvid Institute open letter** wants to publish your name + Halcyon
   Threshold as a signatory, press-facing, by Wednesday. Drafted a
   holding/decline reply in drafts — not sent. Same HR consideration as #3.

5. **Emberfall rapid grant (Idris Bellamy)** — closes 30 Nov, same day as
   your HR disclosure deadline, and requires you as named accountable
   applicant. Drafted a reply saying you intend to apply once a "personal
   admin item" is resolved — not sent. I also started a prep draft of the
   proposal itself in `strategy/` so it's ready fast once you're clear to
   apply.

6. **Priya Raman** offered ~5 hrs/week of help. Drafted a reply giving her a
   concrete, non-public task (funding/opportunity landscape scan) — not
   sent, just needs your okay to go out.

None of the above have been sent/paid/posted. Repo changes (strategy doc,
this file) are in the private repo only.

   Threshold as a signatory, press-facing, by Wednesday. Drafted a

   concrete, non-public task (funding/opportunity landscape scan) — not
   sent, just needs your okay to go out.

None of the above have been sent/paid/posted. Repo changes (strategy doc,
this file) are in the private repo only.
